investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes Unschedulable error: the 6-node swarm cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are fully exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted across all eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 121 s before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a hard contract failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource fully consumed on both eligible nodes: all in-flight or running remote agent pods have claimed the available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pod. Preemption confirms no evictable lower-priority pods exist.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. A misconfigured or missing node label after a node rotation could shrink the eligible pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote agent demand: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have insufficient VM slot capacity for the current workload level, requiring either node scale-out or VM slot quota increase.
Lower confidence — a node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or removed, reducing the eligible pool from a previously larger set to just 2 nodes.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion blocks pod scheduling across all three remote-agent checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval runner for a remote agent type was stuck Unschedulable for 120–150 seconds before the check timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector (likely a label or taint targeting the kata/peerpods runtime class), so even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity existed elsewhere in the cluster it would not be usable by these pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes Unschedulable error: the 6-node swarm cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are fully exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted across all eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 121 s before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a hard contract failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource fully consumed on both eligible nodes: all in-flight or running remote agent pods have claimed the available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pod. Preemption confirms no evictable lower-priority pods exist.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. A misconfigured or missing node label after a node rotation could shrink the eligible pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote agent demand: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have insufficient VM slot capacity for the current workload level, requiring either node scale-out or VM slot quota increase.
Lower confidence — a node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or removed, reducing the eligible pool from a previously larger set to just 2 nodes.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the call that triggers pod scheduling — this call never completed successfully
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all concurrent or recently-created remote agent pods have consumed the available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the total cluster size.

Tertiary — resource leak from prior eval runs or user workloads: if previous remote agent pods were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may not have run to completion on prior failures), their VM slots could still be held, preventing new allocations.

Lower confidence — transient cluster spike: a burst of legitimate remote agent creation by users or other automated processes may have temporarily saturated the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster for current kata.peerpods.io/vm resource utilization on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether capacity is genuinely exhausted or whether pods from prior runs are leaking VM slots.

Review the node affinity and selector configuration on remote agent pods to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional; if not, correcting the affinity rules would expand the schedulable pool and reduce pressure on the 2 eligible nodes.

Audit running and recently-terminated pods associated with the remote-agents workload to check whether the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is reliably releasing VM resources after eval runs, especially on failure paths.

If resource exhaustion is confirmed, determine whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity ceiling on the eligible nodes can be increased (e.g., by adding nodes with the resource, increasing the per-node limit, or scaling the peer-pod provider).

Monitor the next scheduled eval run to determine whether the failure is sustained or self-resolving; the feature registry sets degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187-188), so a second consecutive failure would trigger an outage classification for the remote-agents feature.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), the failure was transient resource contention rather than sustained exhaustion.

If kubectl inspection shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available on the 2 eligible nodes and no pods are currently consuming it, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but a different scheduling or admission failure.

If the node affinity/selector rules were recently changed to exclude more nodes and the 2 remaining nodes have sufficient VM capacity, the affinity misconfiguration would be the primary cause rather than resource exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a concurrent run, the failure would be isolated to the runtime check rather than a shared infrastructure constraint.
If the cluster has more than 2 nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm and the scheduler message is stale or cached, the actual available capacity may differ from what the message reports.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, so resource exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout inside the agent lifecycle checks.

Add a pod-leak detection eval that counts running or pending pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and alerts when the count approaches the node capacity ceiling, catching resource leaks before they cause scheduling failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules meets a minimum threshold, catching affinity misconfigurations that shrink the schedulable pool.

Consider adding a synthetic scheduling dry-run eval (using kubectl --dry-run=server or equivalent) that validates a remote agent pod would be schedulable without actually consuming VM resources, enabling earlier detection of capacity or affinity issues.
